chunks: "A transducer is any device that converts energy from one form to another. A microphone converts sound pressure, which is mechanical energy, into an electrical signal.
A speaker does the opposite. A thermocouple converts heat into voltage, a solar cell converts light into electricity, and a motor converts electrical energy into motion.
The way I keep the terms straight: a transducer is the broad category.
A sensor is a transducer, or a system built around one, whose purpose is measurement, so the output is a signal that carries information about something.
An actuator is a transducer whose purpose is to do something to the world, so electrical energy goes in and mechanical, thermal or acoustic action comes out.
So microphone and thermocouple are input transducers, or sensors, and speaker and heater are output transducers, or actuators.
The practical part is that each transducer has a transfer function, like millivolts per pascal for a MEMS microphone or microvolts per degree for a thermocouple, plus an impedance and a bandwidth.
Those determine the conditioning circuit. A piezo element, for example, has a very high source impedance, so I need a charge amplifier or high-impedance buffer."
